en.title: Hunger Games Director Eyes Plutarch Heavensbee for His Own Spinoff
en.summary: As "Sunrise on the Reaping" prepares for its November 2026 release, director Francis Lawrence is already dreaming up the next potential installment in the "Hunger Games" universe. His sights are set on a character who played a pivotal, albeit complex, role in the original saga.
en.body:
The "Hunger Games" franchise continues to expand its cinematic universe, and director **Francis Lawrence** is already looking ahead. With **"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping"** set to hit theaters on November 20, 2026, Lawrence has revealed his interest in a potential future spinoff centered on **Plutarch Heavensbee**. This ambitious idea emerged during a U.K. fan screening for "Sunrise on the Reaping," where Lawrence shared his thoughts on characters ripe for further exploration.

Lawrence, who has helmed multiple installments in the franchise, including **"The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 1"** and **"Part 2,"** as well as the recent prequel **"The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes,"** expressed his admiration for Plutarch's character depth. He specifically praised **Jesse Plemons**, who takes on the role of Plutarch in "Sunrise on the Reaping," a character originally portrayed by the late **Philip Seymour Hoffman**. "You know, I thought about this," Lawrence stated. "There's so many characters that I love. I think Plutarch [Heavensbee] is a really interesting character, and [co-star Jesse Plemons] just did a tremendous job."

## A New Game Master's Story

The potential for a Plutarch-centric story is particularly intriguing given his evolution within the series. Initially serving as the cunning and manipulative Head Gamemaker, Plutarch later revealed himself to be a key figure in the rebellion against the Capitol. A spinoff focusing on his journey, perhaps detailing his early days in the Games or his clandestine work as a revolutionary, could offer a fascinating perspective on the inner workings of Panem's oppressive regime and the seeds of dissent. This approach mirrors successful prequel expansions in other sci-fi dystopian franchises, like **"Andor"** in the Star Wars universe, which managed to elevate a secondary character into a compelling lead.

## Fans Ready for More Panem

The "Hunger Games" fanbase has consistently shown an appetite for deeper dives into the lore and the complex characters that populate Suzanne Collins' world. The success of **"The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes"** and the anticipation for **"Sunrise on the Reaping"**—which explores the 50th Hunger Games and features a young Haymitch Abernathy—demonstrate a strong desire for stories that flesh out the history and the morally ambiguous figures of Panem. A Plutarch spinoff, especially with **Jesse Plemons** at the helm, would undoubtedly generate significant buzz, offering a chance to explore themes of propaganda, rebellion, and the corrupting nature of power from a unique vantage point.

## What's Next

While the Plutarch Heavensbee spinoff remains a directorial aspiration, **"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping"** is scheduled for release on November 20, 2026. Fans can look forward to seeing **Jesse Plemons**' portrayal of Plutarch and potentially catch glimpses of familiar faces, as **Katniss Everdeen** herself, **Jennifer Lawrence**, has hinted at appearances from **Josh Hutcherson** and **Woody Harrelson**.

content_raw: As The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping nears its November 20 release, its director is sharing ideas for a new spinoff in the Lionsgate franchise—and he already has a Hunger Games character in mind to take the lead. Speaking on the red carpet at a U.K. fan screening of Reaping in late October, director Francis Lawrence said he’s interested in exploring the life of Plutarch Heavensbee, the secret revolutionary in the popular Suzanne Collins series, at some point in the future. “You know, I thought about this,” Lawrence told Lionsgate’s social media team about his dream Games spinoff ( per The Wrap ). “There’s so many characters that I love. I think Plutarch [Heavensbee] is a really interesting character, and [co-star Jesse Plemons] just did a tremendous job.” Plemons took on the role first played by the late Philip Seymour Hoffman in the last three Hunger Games movies to star Jennifer Lawrence. (As for Katniss Everdeen, she recently let slip that she and co-stars Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson will also appear in the new prequel.) “Seeing a Plutarch story would be really interesting,” the director said.  Plemons leading a solo Hunger Games movie would be an interesting move for the franchise. Reaping and Lawrence’s 2023 prequel, The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes also focus on the history of a consequential figure from Katniss Everdeen’s revolutionary era (Joseph Zada’s Haymitch Abernathy and Tom Blyth’s future president Coriolanus Snow, respectively). Plus, other sci-fi dystopian franchises have “reaped” rich ore from their prequel expansions—namely, Tony Gilroy’s Andor , the acclaimed Star Wars prequel that turned a secondary prequel figure into one of the franchise’s richest characters. A Heavensbee-focused prequel with Plemons in the lead could tap into similarly thrilling cloak-and-dagger territory as Andor , with Heavensbee oscillating between his Capitol propaganda work and subversive duties for the rebellion. The idea appeals to Hunger Games producer Nina Jacobsen, who also waxed enthusiastic about the character at the Reaping screening. “I’m a Plutarch obsessive, especially once you read [Collins’ latest book],” she said. “He’s been at this for twenty-five years, playing both sides. Like, how did you pull that off?” You can watch Lawrence and Jacobson talk up Plutarch Heavensbee in an Instagram clip here.
